name: Water pump
summary: Pumps coolant around the engine and the radiator.
whatItDoes: It keeps coolant moving so heat is carried away from the engine to the radiator.
howItWorks: An impeller (a small wheel with curved vanes) spins inside a housing on the engine and pushes coolant through passages in the block and cylinder head. Most water pumps are driven by the timing belt or the accessory belt; some newer engines use electric pumps.
failureSymptoms: Coolant dripping from a small 'weep hole' near the pump
Whining or grinding from the front of the engine
safetyNotes: Let the engine cool completely before draining coolant.
If the timing belt drives the pump, the engine timing must be set correctly when you put it back together.
